name: Ollama
one_liner: Runs open models locally, with a pull-and-run workflow.
what_it_is: A runner for open models, described by its own site as a way to build with open models on your computer and in the cloud. Models are fetched by name and served behind a local HTTP API, so switching model is a pull rather than a rebuild.
why_it_matters: It collapses local model setup to one command, which is why it tends to be where evaluation starts before anything is committed to. What it hides is also its limit: the settings it chooses for you — quantization, context length — are decisions you have not seen, and they matter as soon as you compare results between tools.
suitable_for: Trying a model before committing to an architecture
Local development against a model API
Keeping data on the machine for privacy or policy reasons
not_suitable_for: Cases where you must control quantization and context settings exactly
Reproducibility work, where unseen settings undermine the comparison
